artists.biography:
Anathema are an English band from Liverpool. Beginning as pioneers of the death/doom sub-genre, their later albums have been associated with genres such as alternative rock, progressive rock, art rock, new prog, and post-rock.

Anathema formed in 1990 as a doom metal band, initially going by the name Pagan Angel. In November of that year, the band recorded their first demo, entitled An Iliad of Woes. This demo caught the attention of several bands and labels from the English metal scene.

At the beginning of 1991, the band gained a lot of attention with the release of their second demo entitled All Faith Is Lost, resulting in a four-album deal with Peaceville Records. Their first release under the label was The Crestfallen EP in November 1992. They took the material from that album on the road, touring with Cannibal Corpse.

Serenades, Anathema's debut LP, attracted a lot of mainstream attention, propelling their "Sweet Tears" music video onto the MTV playlist.

Anathema's first European tour was in 1994, and was closely followed by gigs at the Independent Rock Festival in Brazil.

In May 1995, vocalist Darren White parted with the band, eventually forming The Blood Divine. Rather than recruiting a new vocalist, the band decided that guitarist Vincent Cavanagh should assume White's role. This new formation debuted by touring with Cathedral in the United Kingdom.

The release of Eternity came in 1996, relying more on atmospheric sounds, and starting the transition to clean vocals; the album Judgement would later consolidate this style. A European tour followed the album's release.

perplexity.description:
Anathema's Internal Landscapes 2008–2018 (The Best Of) is a compilation album released in 2018 via Kscope, celebrating the band's decade-long partnership with the label. The album collects 13 tracks spanning their most transformative period, drawing from each studio release between We’re Here Because We’re Here (2010) and The Optimist (2017). Musically, it showcases Anathema’s evolution from their heavier, metal-influenced roots into a more atmospheric, melodic, and emotionally resonant style, blending elements of post-progressive rock, alternative rock, and ambient textures. The track selection highlights pivotal moments in their sound, including orchestral and acoustic reinterpretations, and all songs have been newly mastered for a cohesive listening experience.

Within Anathema’s discography, Internal Landscapes serves as both a retrospective and a statement of artistic growth, emphasizing their shift toward introspective songwriting and dynamic arrangements. Critics praised the compilation for its strong curation, noting the seamless flow between tracks and the high quality of songcraft across the decade. Reviewers highlighted the album’s emotional depth, melodic consistency, and the band’s ability to create a unified listening experience despite the material’s chronological spread. While some longtime fans noted omissions, the album was widely regarded as an excellent introduction for new listeners and a rewarding summary of Anathema’s most progressive and accessible era.
